newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki joins U.S.-led rally, but still edgy.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki joins U.S.-led rally, but still edgy.

text.p: Shares rose in an international correction on Tuesday, first nudging ahead in early trade but then jumping after U.S. March inflation data soothed some rate hike nerves, brokers said.
A promising open on Wall Street spurred late activity and some optimism that the rally may continue, but brokers said sentiment remained cautious.

"This looks quite strong, all bourses are up and in fact we are up by slightly less than the others," one broker said. "But we are still on our toes, and we'll watch what the U.S. market does," said another.

The HEX index rose 1.03 percent, the FOX derivatives and portfolio benchmark was up 1.42 percent at 973.78 points. The forestry sub-index rose 1.76 percent, banking added 2.22 percent and the engineering index rose 1.12 percent.
No particular issues stood out, brokers said. Telecoms major Nokia was in line with the market, closing up 3.00 markka at 297.00 and making up just under half total volume.

Forestry major UPM-Kymmene added 2.40 markka to 109.00 and Enso was up 0.90 markka or 2.20 percent at 41.90 markka. Paper machine maker Valmet was among the strongest blue-chips; up 2.20 markka to 88.70 in active 18 million markka trade.
Valmet traded up one markka early on, more than doubling gains after it announced a new tissue machine order from Georgia-Pacific in the U.S.
"The stock has been depressed lately, and is just returning to where it should be," one broker said. Valmet has fallen over seven percent since late February.
The HEX has also fallen about seven percent since its 3,006-point peak on March 11.
